title: Global Poverty Beyond the Official Line: A bounded estimate of material insufficiency
abstract: arXiv:2609.16203v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Numbers this large invite a defensive reflex: reach for the reassuring figure and move on. By the most widely cited measure, the World Bank's extreme-poverty line of \$3.00 per day (2021 PPP), approximately 847 million people, or 10.4% of the world's population, lived in poverty in 2024. That figure is accurate as measured. It is also, by design, a floor: a threshold built to mark bare survival in the poorest economies, not to describe what it takes for a family anywhere to live with basic security.   The central argument of this report is that the reassurance offered by that single line is largely an artifact of how we chose to measure. Held to the \$3.00 floor, roughly 847 million people are poor; held to the standards of their own societies, the number is several times larger, and even the most cautious, honest count exceeds a billion. translated_title: 官方贫困线之外的全球贫困：对物质匮乏的有界估计
translated_abstract: 如此庞大的数字容易引发一种防御性反应：拿起那个令人安心的数字便匆匆翻页。按照最广为引用的衡量标准，即世界银行每天3.00美元（2021年购买力平价）的极端贫困线，2024年约有8.47亿人——占世界人口的10.4%——生活在贫困之中。就测量本身而言，这一数字是准确的。但它从设计上就是一个下限：这一阈值是为标记最贫穷经济体中的勉强生存而设定的，而非描述任何地方一个家庭要过上基本有保障的生活所需要的条件。本报告的核心论点是：这条单一贫困线所提供的安慰，很大程度上是我们选择测量方式所造成的假象。若以3.00美元的下限衡量，约有8.47亿人贫困；若以他们所处社会的标准衡量，这一数字要大数倍，而即便是最谨慎、最诚实的统计也超过10亿。若以适合各国发展水平的收入标准来衡量，约有37亿人陷入贫困。
tldr: 该报告指出世界银行每日3美元的极端贫困线本质上只是一个测量下限，若按适合各国自身发展水平的标准衡量，全球贫困人口实际约为37亿，即使最保守的估计也超过10亿。
en_tdlr: This report argues that the World Bank's $3.00/day extreme poverty line is by design merely a floor, and that measured against standards appropriate to each country's development level, roughly 3.7 billion people live in poverty, with even the most cautious count exceeding one billion.
